In mathematics and [[computer science]], the '''critical exponent''' of a finite or infinite sequence of symbols over a finite alphabet describes the largest number of times a contiguous [[subsequence]] can be repeated.  For example, the critical exponent of "Mississippi" is 7/3, as it contains the string "ississi", which is of length 7 and period 3.

If ''w'' is an infinite word over the alphabet ''A'' and ''x'' is a finite word over ''A'', then ''x'' is said to occur in ''w'' with exponent α, for positive real α, if there is a factor ''y'' of ''w'' with ''y'' = ''x''<sup>''a''</sup>''x''<sub>0</sub> where ''x''<sub>0</sub> is a prefix of ''x'', ''a'' is the integer part of α, and the length |''y''| = α |''x''|: we say that ''y'' is an  ''α-power''.  The word ''w'' is  ''α-power-free'' if it contains no factors which are  β-powers for any β ≥ α.<ref name=K281>{{harvtxt|Krieger|2006}} p.281</ref>

The ''critical exponent'' for ''w'' is the [[supremum]] of the α for which ''w'' has α-powers,<ref name="BLRS126">Berstel et al (2009) p.126</ref> or equivalently the [[infimum]] of the α for which ''w'' is α-power-free.<ref name="K280" />

== Definition ==
If <math>\mathbf{w}</math> is a word (possibly infinite), then the ''critical exponent'' of <math>\mathbf{w}</math> is defined to be
:<math>E(\mathbf{w}) = \sup \{ r \in \mathbb{Q}^{\geq 1} : \mathbf{w} \, \text{ contains an } \, r \text{-power}\}</math> 
where <math>\mathbb{Q}^{\geq 1} = \{ q \in \mathbb{Q} : q \geq 1 \}</math>.<ref>{{Harvard citation text|Krieger|2006}} p.282</ref>

==Examples==
* The critical exponent of the [[Fibonacci word]] is (5&nbsp;+&nbsp;{{radic|5}})/2 ≈ 3.618.<ref name=K280/><ref name =AS37>{{harvtxt|Allouche|Shallit|2003}} p. 37</ref>
* The critical exponent of the [[Thue–Morse sequence]] is 2.<ref name=K280/>  The word contains arbitrarily long squares, but in any factor ''xxb'' the letter ''b'' is not a prefix of ''x''.

==Properties==
* The critical exponent can take any real value greater than 1.<ref name=K280/>{{sfnp|Krieger|Shallit|2007}}
* The critical exponent of a [[morphic word]] over a finite alphabet is either infinite or an [[algebraic number]] of degree at most the size of the alphabet.<ref name=K280>{{harvtxt|Krieger|2006}} p.280</ref>

==Repetition threshold==
The '''repetition threshold''' of an alphabet ''A'' of ''n'' letters is the minimum critical exponent of infinite words over ''A'': clearly this value RT(''n'') depends only on ''n''.  For ''n''=2, any binary word of length four has a factor of exponent 2, and since the critical exponent of the Thue–Morse sequence is 2, the repetition threshold for binary alphabets is RT(2) = 2.  It is known that RT(3) = 7/4, RT(4) = 7/5 and that RT(''n'') = ''n''/(''n''-1) for ''n'' ≥ 5.
<ref name=BLRS126/><ref name=AS37/>
